spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Double Mellin inversion factorizes a higher zeta moment through two lower transforms and reveals a coupled-frequency constraint, while the modified-transform product law compresses the same structure into a vertical convolution recurrence for Z_{k+l}.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For m=k+l, equation (7.6) inserts the inversion formula first for Z_k and then for Z_l into a smoothly localized 2m-th moment, producing a triple integral in s, w, and x. Repeated integration by parts in x shows that only coupled frequencies with |Im(w)+Im(s)| small on the stated scale contribute nontrivially, and gives a moment bound T^{c+d-1} when the contours and triple integral converge. Lemma 2 also gives Z_m(s)=(2 pi i)^{-1} integral Z_l(w)Z_k(s+1-w)dw on a sufficiently far-right line.
directed.conceptual_reading: The factorization makes the hierarchy compositional: multiplication of moment densities becomes convolution of their modified Mellin transforms. The localized triple integral additionally exposes which pairs of transform frequencies can interact.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridges are smooth double Mellin inversion, integration-by-parts frequency localization, and the recurrence Z_{k+l}=Z_l convolved with a shifted Z_k.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Useful consequences require contours c and d for which all integrals converge and separate bounds on the lower transforms. The recurrence is an algebraic framework, not by itself an improved moment estimate; it also shows that sigma>=1 can remain relevant.
directed.uncertainty: Nested contours, variables, powers, the frequency condition, and the exact shift s+1-w are heavily line-broken. Exact formulas (7.6)-(7.7) require PDF verification.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The known eighth-moment lower scale is fed through the k=l=2 factorization and the discrete spectral part of Z_2, producing a heuristic lower bound of square-root size for the same unit-window oscillatory Hecke sums in Conjecture 3.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source sets m=4 and k=l=2 in (7.6), uses the lower scale T log^{16}T for the localized eighth moment, truncates the s-integral through derivative mean bounds, and isolates the discrete-spectrum contribution on a shifted w-line. Integration by parts localizes to |t+kappa_j|<=|t|^epsilon. It then uses the heuristic implication from Conjecture 3 to pointwise Conjecture 2 to truncate t, applies Stirling to R_1, subdivides the spectrum into unit intervals, and extracts suprema to motivate (7.8), a lower bound of order T^{1/2-epsilon} for a phased central-Hecke sum.
directed.conceptual_reading: The argument is an optimality stress test: if the conjectured cancellation controls the auxiliary transform strongly enough, the independently large eighth moment forces some unit spectral packet back up to square-root scale. Thus a substantially smaller universal upper scale would conflict with the same heuristic framework.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge chain is eighth-moment lower bound -> double-transform factorization -> discrete spectral residues -> phase localization and Stirling -> supremum over unit spectral sums.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is explicitly heuristic and partially assumes Conjecture 3 through its proposed implication to Conjecture 2; it is not a proved omega result and should not be reported as independent evidence for the conjecture. Truncation, interchange, and trivial supremum extraction all carry unresolved proof burdens.
directed.uncertainty: The supremum range, phase constant C, spectral localization, nested integral, R_1 asymptotic, and final exponent are extraction-damaged. Equation (7.8) and every transition require PDF verification.
